# Changelog

**Spoolman NG** is a community-maintained fork of [Spoolman](https://github.com/Donkie/Spoolman) by Donkie. Full per-release notes (auto-generated from merged pull requests) are published on the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/sherrmann/Spoolman-NG/releases) page; this file summarizes notable changes.

## Unreleased

- **Fixed: every SQLite backup leaked two database connections, and backup rotation could fail on Windows** (ported from upstream) — a `sqlite3.Connection` used as a context manager commits on exit but never closes, so the two handles the backup opens stayed open for the life of the process. The visible consequence is Windows-only: rotation moves the file the backup just wrote, and the still-open handle makes that fail with "used by another process". POSIX lets you move an open file, so no Linux install ever noticed, which is also why the existing rotation tests passed throughout. The new test asserts the connections are closed rather than asserting that rotation works, since the latter cannot fail on the platform CI runs.

- **Fixed: the container would not start on Kubernetes behind a Service named `spoolman`** (ported from upstream) — Kubernetes injects a Docker-style service link for every Service in the namespace at pod start, so that name sets `SPOOLMAN_PORT=tcp://<clusterIP>:8000`. That is the Service address rather than a port, and uvicorn refuses to bind it, so the container failed to start citing a port nobody had configured — the value came from the cluster, not from any values file. Such a value is now ignored with a warning and the default port used instead. This fork ships a Helm chart, so it presents exactly the deployment shape that triggers it.

- **Added: switch between the two web clients from inside the UI** — this fork ships both the classic React client and the newer Svelte one, but which one you got was an operator decision fixed at startup (`SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT`), so trying the other meant editing an environment variable and restarting the server, for everyone at once. An **Interface** control now sits with the other appearance settings in both clients, and switching takes a click and a reload. The choice is stored in a cookie, so it is per browser: one person can stay on the classic UI while another tries the new one on the same instance. Every URL is unchanged either way — deep links, bookmarks and printed QR labels all keep working, because both clients are served at the same paths and only the cookie decides which answers. `SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT` keeps its name and meaning and now sets the default for browsers that have not chosen; operators who would rather everyone saw one UI can set `SPOOLMAN_UI_SWITCHER=FALSE`, which hides the control and ignores any cookie already stored. Switching to the Svelte client also tears down the React client's service worker on the way out, so the old cached shell cannot come back. The control hides itself where there is nothing to switch to — an install from source that built only one client — and inside an installed PWA, whose manifest belongs to the client it was installed from. The release zip now carries both clients, as the Docker image already did, so a native install can serve either one and switch between them too -- previously it shipped only the React bundle (and, oddly, the whole unbuilt Svelte source), so `SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT=FALSE` could not work there at all.

- **Added: voice input, natural-language search and an AI settings panel in the Svelte client** — the last three AI surfaces the opt-in Svelte client was missing. **Voice**: hold a button in the assistant to dictate, and optionally have replies read back; a transcript lands in the box to review before it is sent, unless you turn that off. **Natural-language search**: describe the spools you want ("black PETG on shelf B") and it fills in the Library's ordinary filter chips, which you can then edit or remove like any others — and it tells you when part of your search could not be applied here, rather than quietly returning more than you asked for. **Settings**: an operator panel for the endpoint, models, keys and speech-to-text, with a connection test that reports what the endpoint actually supports, one-click Ollama model pulls, and per-feature switches that explain what is missing instead of failing later. Every feature remains off by default. The panel is shown only to administrators — a read-only user previously saw a form they were never allowed to save.

- **Added: the AI assistant in the Svelte client** — the opt-in Svelte client gains this fork's chat assistant as a drawer: ask about your inventory in plain language, and it answers by running read queries against your own data, showing which ones it ran. It can also make changes — moving a spool, creating a filament, placing an order — but never on its own: a proposed change stops the conversation and shows a before/after card listing exactly which fields move, and nothing is written until you approve it. Deletions are marked as irreversible, and a change that can be undone offers a one-click undo. Like every AI surface in this fork it is **off by default and completely invisible until an operator turns it on** — no button, no placeholder. Translated in 26 languages, from the React client's existing catalogue. Voice input and spoken replies are a separate feature and are not ported yet.

- **Added: write a spool onto an NFC tag from the Svelte client** — the opt-in Svelte client can link a tag by its UID but never had any way to put a spool's data *on* one. A new "Encode to NFC" action on a spool's tag section offers all three routes this fork's React client has: a reader attached to the Spoolman host writes the raw bytes (the only route that produces a tag the TigerTag app recognises, and the only one that can write Qidi at all); this phone writes over Web NFC, which can only emit NDEF and so produces a tag the app will not recognise — said plainly on screen before you commit; or the same bytes download as a file for an external tool, which needs no reader and no radio and is therefore what desktop and iOS users get. Translated in 26 languages, from the React client's existing catalogue.

- **Added: scan-to-move, retail barcodes and the clear-spool code in the Svelte client** — the opt-in Svelte client's QR scanner previously did one thing: open whatever was scanned. It now also does the three things this fork's React scanner does. **Move spool** is a two-scan flow — scan a spool, then scan a shelf label, confirm, and the spool is moved there, so re-shelving is a camera job rather than a search-and-edit one. A **manufacturer's own UPC/EAN barcode** on the spool is looked up by article number: a match opens Add-spools already on that filament, and no match offers to create one that remembers the barcode, so the next scan of that spool resolves by itself. And the reserved **`WEB+SPOOLMAN:CLEAR`** code is now acknowledged rather than looking like a dud label — Spoolman holds no active spool of its own, so the message says which part of your setup does. Translated in 26 languages, from the React client's existing catalogue.

- **Added: the fork's browser tests can drive a real camera** — the scan flows above are wiring more than logic, and wiring is what a unit test cannot see. `tests_frontend_ng` now synthesises a QR video and hands it to Chromium as the camera, so the tests scan actual labels through the actual scanner: a spool code still reaching upstream's own navigation, a spool label followed by a shelf label really moving the spool in the database, and a barcode arriving mid-move being ignored rather than losing the half-finished move.

- **Added: an Orders page in the Svelte client** — the opt-in Svelte client (`SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT=FALSE`) gains this fork's Orders page at `/orders`: every order with its shop, date, how many of its lines have arrived and whether it is still open; opening one to edit its header and line quantities, delete it, or mark lines arrived — in full or as a partial delivery that splits the line — optionally creating the spools at a chosen location. New orders can be built from scratch. The "Ordered" pill on Low Stock and Home now links here and names the shop, which it could not do before this page existed. Translated in 26 languages, from the React client's existing catalogue.

- **Added: a Low Stock page in the Svelte client, with its reorder workflow** — the opt-in Svelte client (`SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT=FALSE`) gains this fork's Low Stock page at `/lowstock`: filaments below their own threshold and below the global default, each row showing what is left, whether it is already on order, and controls to adjust the threshold or mark it ordered — plus selecting several rows and raising one order for the lot. Shops are picked by name and created on the spot if new. This is the first Svelte page in the fork that writes rather than reads, and the same controls now work on the Home dashboard's Low Stock tab, which shipped read-only. Translated in 26 languages, from the React client's existing catalogue.

- **Added: browser tests for this fork's own pages in the Svelte client** — the vendored suite (`tests_frontend_v2`) covers upstream's pages, and nothing covered the fork's. That gap had already cost something: the new Home page shipped with a layout defect that svelte-check, eslint, prettier and 344 unit tests all passed over, because it was one missing CSS class and only visible in a real browser at a short window. `tests_frontend_ng` now drives the page against a real backend and asserts what actually broke — that the page scrolls inside the app shell rather than overflowing it — alongside checks that the summary cards match what the API returns, that every tab renders, that a filament already on order is marked as such, and that no request or console error is failing silently behind a populated-looking panel. It gates releases like the other suites.
- **Added: a Home dashboard in the Svelte client** — the opt-in Svelte client (`SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT=FALSE`) gains this fork's Home page at `/home`: stock, filament, manufacturer and total-weight summaries, breakdowns by material, manufacturer and location, recently-used and long-idle spool lists, and the filament-usage chart. It is the first of the fork's own pages to exist in both clients; the React client remains the default and is unchanged. The page arrives translated in 26 languages rather than English-only, because its strings are generated from the React client's existing catalogue instead of being written again. The Low Stock tab is read-only for now — marking a filament as ordered and editing its threshold arrive with the Low Stock page itself.

## [2026.8.2] — 2026-08-26

- **Fixed: a group's total remaining weight could come back with float drift** — `GET /spool/group` summed remaining weight as a raw float, the one weight expression that skipped the rounding every other weight calculation uses, so a group holding an exact 2997.9 g could report 2997.8999999999996.
- **Added: browser tests for the Svelte client** — upstream's Playwright suite is now vendored and runs in CI against a real backend, covering CRUD, search, labels, tags, settings, spool overrides, the PWA and service-worker behaviour. 47 of its 48 tests pass against this fork unmodified, which says more about how closely the APIs now line up than the porting work's own tests could: they were written against upstream's backend and had never seen this one. The exception is a date-range filter this fork deliberately does not implement.
- **Fixed: the Docker integration matrix aborted on an unmarked async test** — the tester container mounts only `tests_integration/tests` and installs four pinned packages, so it never sees this repo's `pyproject.toml` and its `asyncio_mode = "auto"`. pytest-asyncio therefore ran in its default strict mode there, where an `async def` test with no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` is not skipped but *failed*, and the tester's `--exitfirst` turned the first one into a dead matrix leg. Ten such tests in the new tag relay suite passed locally and could only ever have failed in CI. They are now marked, and a check in the fast suite asserts that every async test in the Docker suite carries the marker, so the next one is caught in seconds rather than a CI round trip.
- **Changed: CI streams container output instead of swallowing it** — the integration matrix ran through an action that buffers every container's output and, on failure, prints only a byte-capped excerpt from the *start* of the run, so the message explaining the failure was truncated away entirely. It has cost two diagnosis cycles that way. Compose now runs inline with its output streaming into the job log as it happens, the exit code comes from the tester rather than whichever container stopped first, and a failed run additionally dumps every container's full timestamped log.
- **Fixed: the Svelte client's Labels and Dashboard pages could not save anything** — the label designer and the dashboard's grouping store their state in server settings, and this fork had never registered the keys they use, because the React client does not use them. Every read and write returned 404, so a label design could not be saved at all and dashboard grouping could not persist; both pages failed into empty states rather than erroring, which is why it went unnoticed. `label_designs`, `dashboard_groups` and `dashboard_spoolorders` are now registered with upstream's exact keys, types and defaults, so the vendored client works unmodified. A saved design is around 1.3 KB, and the existing 65,535-character setting limit holds roughly fifty of them, so no limit needed raising.
- **Fixed: a CSV export could run a formula when opened in a spreadsheet** (CWE-1236, ported from upstream) — Excel and LibreOffice treat a cell beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return as a formula, and the CSV export wrote user-supplied text straight through. Anyone who could set a vendor name, spool comment, location or extra-field value — including an integration writing over the API — could put `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0` in your inventory and have it execute on whoever opened the export. String cells are now prefixed with a single quote, which spreadsheets read as "this is literal text" and do not display. Numbers are left alone, so a negative price stays a number. The JSON export is unchanged, since JSON has no such behaviour. **This affected released versions of the fork, not just unreleased work.**
- **Fixed: `%` and `_` in a search or filter matched every row instead of themselves** (ported and extended from upstream) — both characters are SQL `LIKE` wildcards, and they were passed through unescaped, so searching for `50%` quietly returned the entire inventory rather than the one spool whose comment says `50%`. Upstream's fix covered its own two query paths; this fork had three more it does not have — the shared `?name=`/`?location=`/`?material=` filters, and the separate `search=` fuzzy match on spools and filaments — which are fixed here too.
- **Fixed: an oversized setting value returned a 500 instead of a 400** (ported from upstream) — the length limit was enforced in the database layer but the endpoint never caught the resulting error, so writing too large a value produced an unhandled server error rather than a message saying what was wrong.
- **Fixed: the settings endpoint accepted any content type** (ported from upstream) — a plain HTML form can post `text/plain` cross-origin without a CORS preflight, so accepting it widened the surface for no benefit. The endpoint now requires `application/json` and answers 415 otherwise.
- **Fixed: an unusual base path could break the generated `config.js`** (ported from upstream) — the base path was hand-quoted into a JavaScript string with a guard that only rejected a double quote, so a path ending in a backslash escaped the closing quote and broke out of the literal. The value is now JSON-encoded, which is correct for any input, and the guard is no longer needed.
- **Added: upstream's Svelte client ships alongside the React one, as an opt-in preview** — upstream rewrote its frontend from scratch in Svelte and now serves it by default; that client is vendored here as a git subtree so its improvements can be pulled rather than reimplemented. **The React client remains the default and is unchanged** — it still covers thirteen page groups to the Svelte client's five, so nothing about the normal experience moves. Set `SPOOLMAN_LEGACY_CLIENT=FALSE` to serve the Svelte client instead. The variable keeps upstream's name and meaning (`TRUE` = React) so it does not mean different things in the two projects; only the default differs. Both clients are built into the Docker image. Two of the Svelte client's pages — Dashboard grouping and the label designer — depend on settings this fork has not registered yet and are not yet functional; the rest, including the new search, works against this backend.
- **Changed: NFC tag bindings now live in the `tag` table, keyed on the physical tag UID** — the fork previously bound a tag to a spool by writing a hidden `nfc_tag_id` extra field whose value was a *synthesized* identity, different for every tag standard: a product-and-timestamp pair for TigerTag, an instance UUID for OpenPrintTag, a payload hash for tags with no identity at all. That is now replaced by the same `tag` table upstream uses, so a spool's tags are real rows that any client can read, link and unlink through the documented API instead of a private field only this fork understood. A spool can still carry several tags; each is bound once, by its own UID. **Existing bindings mostly do not survive this.** Only Qidi bindings stored the physical UID and are converted automatically; TigerTag, OpenPrintTag and payload-hash bindings never contained a UID and cannot be reconstructed, so **those spools need to be rescanned once**. The old rows are deliberately left in the database rather than deleted, and the upgrade logs exactly how many were converted and how many were left behind. The `/api/v1/nfc/*` endpoints and their response shapes are unchanged, so the mobile app, browser scanner and Klipper daemons keep working.
- **Changed: `POST /api/v1/nfc/lookup` with `auto_create` now requires `nfc_tag_uid`** — a spool created from a scan is found again by the UID of the tag that created it, so a request that asks to auto-create without supplying one has nothing to bind the new spool to, and every identical rescan would quietly create another spool. The request is now refused with a message naming the missing field. Every real reader — the browser scanner, the USB reader, the mobile app — already sends the UID; a caller that does not has a bug, and being told about it is better than watching an inventory fill up with duplicates.
- **Added: group the spool list by filament, vendor, material, location or an extra field** (ported from upstream) — `GET /api/v1/spool/group` returns one row per group with the aggregates a summary view actually needs: how many spools, how many are in use, the total weight remaining and when the group was last used. It takes the same filters as the spool list, including filtering by a *filament's* or *vendor's* extra fields, and reports the full count in `x-total-count` so a client can page through groups.
- **Added: rename an extra-field value everywhere it occurs** (ported from upstream) — `PATCH /api/v1/spool/field/{field}` renames one value of a spool's `location` or an `extra.*` field across the whole inventory in a single call, archived spools included, which is where a typo would otherwise sit forever because the list view hides them. Renaming onto a value that already exists merges the two groups rather than creating a duplicate.
- **Added: list the values in use for an extra field** — `GET /api/v1/field/{entity}/{key}/values` returns the distinct values actually stored for a field, which is what a filter menu needs in order to offer choices rather than a free-text box.
- **Added: `external_db_name` on `GET /api/v1/info`** — clients can now name the filament database an instance is pointed at instead of assuming it is the default one, which matters for this fork because it defaults to its own SpoolmanDB rather than upstream's.
- **Changed: `POST /api/v1/backup` now reports whether it actually wrote one, and stops rotating identical copies** (ported from upstream) — the response gains `created`, and a backup is skipped when the database has not changed since the last one or when one was taken within the previous five minutes. Without this, repeatedly hitting the endpoint would roll every genuinely useful backup out of the retention window and replace it with identical copies of the same moment. Scheduled and startup backups are unaffected.
- **Added: one search across spools, filaments and vendors** (ported from upstream) — `GET /api/v1/search?q=...` answers in a single call instead of making a client query three endpoints and stitch the results together. Terms are whitespace-split and ANDed, so `Bambu PETG-CF` matches only what satisfies both, and matching covers extra fields as well as the built-in text ones; every hit says which field it matched on. A purely numeric query resolves a spool by id. A query that names a colour — a hex code like `#FF0000` or a CSS name like `red` — switches to perceptual colour matching (CIE Lab, delta-E) with a tunable `color_similarity_threshold`, so "red" finds filaments that look red rather than only ones with "red" in the name. Filament hits can carry their first few spools via `spools_per_filament`. This is the surface upstream's client and other API consumers now expect. The fork's own indexed `color_hue` filter is a separate feature and is unchanged.
- **Changed: the extra-field engine is now upstream's, with this fork's extensions carried over** (ported from upstream) — while the two projects were diverged they each built the same two modules for querying extra fields, incompatibly. Upstream's is the larger and is what its search and grouping features are built on, so this fork adopts it as the base rather than maintaining a permanent divergence in the middle of the query layer. Nothing about the API changes: the fork's `location` and `printer` entity types, its `link` field type, `link_template` and `copy_from_filament` all carry over, and extra-field filtering, sorting and range queries were re-verified over HTTP against spools, filaments, vendors, locations and printers. What comes with it is capability the next changes need — reusable join helpers, filtering spools by their filament's or vendor's extra fields, distinct-value lookup for grouping, and MySQL-specific JSON handling the fork previously lacked.
- **Fixed: a malformed extra-field definition written through the generic settings endpoint wedged `GET /field/{entity}` into a permanent 500** (ported from upstream) — `POST /setting/extra_fields_*` validated that the value was a string but never that it was a well-formed field array, so a bad write was accepted and then failed to parse on every subsequent read, with no way back through the UI. Such a write is now rejected with a 400. The same endpoint also now invalidates the in-memory field cache, so a definition written through settings is visible to `GET /field/{entity}` immediately rather than after the next restart. Other settings keys are unaffected.
- **Added: NFC tags are now first-class rows, with a scan relay for hardware readers** (ported from upstream) — a new `tag` table records the UID a physical tag carries and what it points at, reachable through `POST`/`DELETE /api/v1/spool/{id}/tag`, a `tag=` filter on the spool search, and a new `/api/v1/tag` router with `POST /tag/scan`, `GET /tag/reader` and websocket subscriptions at `WS /tag/scan[/{reader_id}]`. The relay is transport-agnostic: anything that can make one HTTP POST — an ESP32 at the printer, a PN532 on a Pi, Node-RED, a phone — can report a scan and have every open browser react to it, with a 3-second debounce keyed on the resolved match so a tag left sitting on a reader does not spam subscribers. `scripts/fake_reader.py` (`uv run poe fake-reader`) drives the whole path without any hardware. This is the identity layer upstream shipped; **the fork's existing NFC subsystem is untouched by this change** and still binds tags through its own `nfc_tag_uid` field — moving it onto this table is a separate change. `POST /tag/scan` is not exempt from `SPOOLMAN_API_TOKEN`, matching how every other unattended writer (Moonraker's `use`/`measure`, the NFC `lookup`/`bind` routes) is already treated.
- **Added: cross-origin writes and websocket handshakes are now refused by default** (ported from upstream) — Spoolman NG's own authentication is opt-in, and even where it is switched on it gates individual endpoints rather than the transport, so on the overwhelming majority of deployments the network was the only thing protecting a user's inventory. That is a weaker boundary than it sounds: an HTML form post needs no CORS preflight, and a websocket handshake is exempt from CORS entirely, so any page a user happened to visit could write to — or, over the websocket, read from — a Spoolman instance their browser could reach. A `TrustedOriginMiddleware` now rejects unsafe methods and websocket handshakes whose `Origin` is neither the instance's own nor listed in `SPOOLMAN_CORS_ORIGIN`. **Non-browser clients are deliberately unaffected**: Moonraker, OctoPrint, curl and the NFC Klipper daemons send no `Origin` header at all, and an absent header is trusted by design, so nothing that talks to Spoolman today stops working. `X-Forwarded-Host` is honoured so that nginx and Apache setups which rewrite `Host` don't see the guard reject their own web UI. Opt out with `SPOOLMAN_CORS_ORIGIN=*`.
- **Added: an opt-in DNS-rebinding guard** (ported from upstream) — set `SPOOLMAN_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (comma-separated, leading `*.` for subdomains) and requests addressed to any other hostname are refused. Off by default, and deliberately so: the hostnames it would otherwise have to reject — IP addresses, single-label names, `*.local` — are exactly the ones an outside attacker cannot point at a home LAN, so the common deployment needs no configuration. It is worth setting if you reach Spoolman through a public domain name behind a reverse proxy.
- **Fixed: `SPOOLMAN_CORS_ORIGIN=*` no longer advertises that credentials may be sent** — the wildcard was previously combined with `allow_credentials=True`, which makes Starlette echo the caller's origin back and set `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, telling the browser it may send cookies to whichever site asked. Spoolman NG has no cookies of its own — its bearer tokens are attached explicitly rather than carried automatically — but plenty of instances sit behind a reverse proxy that authenticates with one, and there the combination let any site the user visited make authenticated requests as them. Credentialed cross-origin requests are now refused whenever the origin list is `*`. **This is a behaviour change** for anyone relying on that combination; name your origins explicitly instead of using `*`.
- **Fixed: a comma-separated `SPOOLMAN_CORS_ORIGIN` silently ignored every entry after the first** — the value was split on commas with no trimming, so `https://a, https://b` produced an entry with a leading space that could never match an `Origin` header. Entries are now normalized and de-duplicated.

## [2026.8.1] — 2026-08-25

- **Fixed: any non-UI client could permanently break the spool list with one bad write** (#377 follow-up) — Spoolman is written to by Moonraker, OctoPrint, Home Assistant, NFC tooling, the mobile app and third-party clients, none of which go through the web UI that #383 fixed, and nothing validated what they sent. `Infinity` and `NaN` are not valid JSON, but Python's `json.loads` — which Starlette uses to read request bodies — accepts both as bare literals, and pydantic's `allow_inf_nan` defaults to True, so they passed validation and were persisted. On the way back out Starlette renders with `json.dumps(allow_nan=False)`, which raises: **a single such row made every response containing that spool fail with an unhandled 500**, so the spool list stayed broken in every browser until the row was repaired by hand. `PUT /spool/{id}/use` — the endpoint Moonraker calls on every print — had no constraints on `use_weight` at all, not even `ge=0`. The spool request models now reject non-finite floats and bound every weight at `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which is not an arbitrary sanity limit but exactly where the browser stops deserializing a numeric literal as a number (#69); `use_*` deltas stay signed, since a negative one is a legitimate refill. Rejecting rather than clamping is deliberate — a client sending `Infinity` has a bug, and a 422 says so, where silently storing a plausible substitute would keep the broken integration quiet while corrupting inventory. Two things fell out of fixing it: the 422 itself was **unrenderable**, because the validation payload echoes the offending `inf` straight back into the same strict encoder, turning a clean rejection into another 500 — the API now sanitises non-finite values out of error payloads; and the in-process test harness built a bare `FastAPI()` with none of the real app's exception handlers, so no test could ever have caught either 500. It now installs the same validation handler production uses.
- **Fixed: an oversized weight already in the database could still corrupt the dashboard totals, and nothing ever repaired one** (#377 follow-up) — #383 closed the path that *created* these values, but not the one that reads them back. A weight that is a whole number beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is the single case the browser's deserializer still returns as a **string** on purpose: that is the rule which keeps oversized CockroachDB ids exact (#69), and it is applied per value rather than per field, so it catches a weight column just the same. Reading such a row flipped the home page's `sum + spoolStockWeight(s)` reduce back into string concatenation — the original #377 defect, reachable again from data alone. `spoolStockWeight` now coerces once with the same `Number()` + `Number.isFinite` pattern the weight formatters use; it is the single funnel every dashboard aggregate draws from, so that is the only place the guard is needed. The three remaining bare `.toFixed()` call sites were checked and are **not** reachable — the label formatter already tests `typeof value === "number"`, the weight-history chart is fed by a `measureSeries` that filters on the same, and the usage-history table is fetched with native `response.json()`, which never yields a string for a numeric literal. Separately, a **new migration repairs rows poisoned before the fix shipped**, which nothing did until now: values past the safe-integer bound (9e15 grams is nine billion tonnes, so no legitimate row is in range) are **cleared, not corrected** — nullable weight columns become NULL, the two NOT NULL columns fall back to zero. The true value is unrecoverable, and a plausible-looking invented number would bury the damage where nobody would question it, whereas a blank field gets noticed and fixed. Data-only, so it applies cleanly under CockroachDB's transactional DDL; the downgrade is deliberately a no-op.

## [2026.8.0] — 2026-08-20

- **Fixed: the assistant looked up filament IDs the user had just given it, and the eval could not see fabricated arguments** (#380) — `create_order`'s description said "every filament must already exist (use create_filament first)", and models read that as an instruction to go and verify: asked to *"record an order of 2x filament 6"*, they searched for what "filament 6" meant or stopped to ask for an ID the user had already supplied. Scoping the lookup to the case that needs it (a filament named but not yet created) takes `gemma4:e2b` from a reproducible **1/4 to 2/4** on the order fixtures, measured three times per wording; `qwen3:4b-instruct` was already at 3/4 and is unchanged. Separately, `poe ai-eval` now reports **invented arguments** — string values the model supplied that appear nowhere in the prompt. It was blind to these: one model scored a clean pass on `create_order` while fabricating a shop, an order number, a date and a comment, *and* dropping the price that really was in the prompt — an order attributed to a shop the user never named, looking like a success in every other column. Enum members and derived values (a date range computed from "last month", a hex code from a colour word) are exempt, since flagging those buried the real cases in noise.
- **Fixed: a misread label could write impossible values straight into a spool** (#380) — extraction is now checked against what filament physically is before anything downstream sees it. Measured models really did return `weight_g: 1750` (the label's "1.75MM" read as a weight), a 65 °C nozzle for PETG, a **220 °C bed for PLA**, `vendor: "FIRE ENGINE RED"` (the colour, in a field the matcher weights at 0.3), `vendor: "SILVER-1KG(N.W)"` — the last two reported with `confidence: "high"` — and the material echoed back as the product name. `name`, `vendor`, `material` and `weight_g` are the only fields `score_candidate` weights, so a confident mistake there quietly drags the match toward the wrong filament; the temperatures land in the record the user saves. Values are dropped, never corrected — a blank field gets fixed on the confirm card, a wrong one does not get noticed. The rules stop at *impossible*, not *unusual*: temperature windows are wider than any vendor's recommendation (a 50 °C PETG bed is low but real, so it survives), the weight rule targets the specific diameter-as-weight confusion rather than banding plausible weights, and vendors are **not** required to appear in the catalog — "Prusa Polymers" is the right answer on a Prusament label but not the catalog's spelling, and small brands are absent entirely. Replayed against the verbatim output of every model measured, this removes 9 wrong values and **0 correct ones**. `confidence` is deliberately not used as a filter, having been reported "high" alongside a colour name in the vendor field. It catches values that are impossible, not values that are merely wrong: a garbled product name still gets through.
- **Changed: the recommended-model shortlist now reflects what was actually measured** (#380) — the Settings → AI list was written from model cards, not from running anything. Most consequentially it recommended **`qwen3:4b`**, whose `-instruct` sibling is a different model: measured against the 19-tool layer, plain `qwen3:4b` selects the right tool 76% of the time at ~21 s per call, while **`qwen3:4b-instruct` scores 91% at ~1.9 s** — 15 accuracy points and an 11× speed difference hanging off a suffix. The entry now names the `-instruct` build and says why. **`granite4.1:3b` is added** (85-87%, ~0.7 s, the only candidate that fits a 4 GB GPU entirely, and — having no thinking capability at all — structurally immune to the Ollama default above). **`qwen3:8b` is no longer "the default recommendation"**: it wants ~6 GB of VRAM and spills to CPU below that, which is the opposite of a safe default. **`qwen2.5vl:7b` keeps its place** — it had never been benchmarked, and it turns out to be the best local label reader tested: it read every photo and was the only one that never wrote a wrong value into the four fields that decide which filament a scan matches. The size field is renamed `downloadSizeGb`, because that is all it is: Gemma's E-series offloads Per-Layer Embeddings, so `gemma4:e2b` is a 7.2 GB download that runs in 1.7 GB, and presenting a download size as a hardware requirement would steer people away from models their machine handles fine.
- **Fixed: the tool-selection eval scored instructed behaviour as failure, and had one fixture that contradicted the system prompt** (#380) — the prompt tells the model to look before it writes ("check `find_vendors` or `find_locations` before creating a vendor or location that may already exist"; never invent a density, call `catalog_lookup`), but `poe ai-eval` was single-turn: a model that followed that instruction never reached the write and scored **zero** on those cases. It penalised careful models hardest — one frontier model lost every one of its misses this way while following the prompt exactly. Fixtures can now declare the precursor calls that legitimately come first; the harness feeds back a synthetic result and scores the second call, and reports **completed task** separately from **directly**. A *wrong* first tool never earns a second turn, so the follow-up cannot become a retry that launders bad tool selection into a pass. The synthetic results are chosen to leave exactly one sensible next step — an empty vendor list, and a catalog hit carrying the density and diameter the prompt forbids guessing. One fixture ("Add the Sunlu PLA Meta black…") expected `create_filament` while supplying neither density nor diameter, which is precisely the case the prompt says to look up first; it now supplies both, so the expected call is genuinely correct. **New: `poe ai-eval-vision`** does the same job for Scan-to-Spool, running label photos through `spoolintake.extract` itself — the photo path previously had no automated coverage against a real model at all, and its failure mode is silent. It reports field accuracy overall and for the four fields that actually decide whether a scan finds the right filament. Only a synthetic label ships with the repo (a floor test); point it at your own photos with `--photos`.
- **Fixed: Ollama silently turned thinking on, costing tool accuracy and breaking Scan-to-Spool outright** (#380) — Ollama auto-enables thinking for any model whose capabilities include `thinking` when a request carries no reasoning control, and Spoolman sent none. Measured against the curated 19-tool layer on 55 fixture prompts, that default cost **15–21 points of tool-selection accuracy and ran 3–7× slower** across three model families (`qwen3.5:4b` 75%→60%, `qwen3.5:2b` 56%→35%, `gemma4:e2b` 78%→62%); on the photo path it pushed **every** extraction past the request timeout, so Scan-to-Spool could not complete a single label — including a flat, perfectly-framed one — on a thinking-capable vision model. Requests to a positively-identified Ollama endpoint now send `reasoning_effort: "none"` when, and only when, the model itself advertises `thinking`; `think` and `chat_template_kwargs` are accepted and ignored on Ollama's OpenAI-compatible surface, so neither is a substitute. Photo extraction additionally asks for `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`, which took the best local vision model from 4 of 6 label photos to **6 of 6** at roughly half the latency — the failures were spending their time generating prose we then discarded. Both keys are Ollama-specific and gated on the model's advertised capabilities, so a **generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint receives exactly the body it received before** — asserted by its own test, because a strict server is entitled to reject an unknown key. The capability lookup is memoised per model, and every failure path falls back to today's payload: it is an optimisation on the request path and must never be able to fail a real request. The photo path also gets a longer timeout than a chat turn (a 1568 px label costs ~1,800 image tokens to decode before generation starts, and Spoolman targets CPU-only NASes and Pis).
- **Fixed: the home page crashed, and weight totals were silently wrong, once any spool weight carried float64 noise** (#377) — `json-bigint`'s "keep long numbers as strings" rule gates on the raw literal's *length* (>15 characters), not on whether it is an integer, so an ordinary gram value such as `0.30000000000000004` (19 characters) arrived in the browser as a **string** despite its declared number type. The dashboard then computed `sum + weight`, and one string operand turns `+` into concatenation: every subsequent spool's weight was appended as digits rather than added — that, not any stored value, is where the reported 55-digit total came from. Sub-1000-gram values reached `.toFixed()` as strings and took the whole render tree down with `TypeError: e.toFixed is not a function`. Long literals now arrive as `BigNumber` and are revived one at a time, so only whole numbers beyond the safe-integer range become strings — the CockroachDB large-id behavior (#69) is preserved exactly. The weight and length formatters additionally coerce defensively, so no future unexpected value can crash a page, and `used_weight` is rounded to 6 decimals on every write path — six rather than one, to strip representation noise without discarding the genuine sub-gram increments a slicer reports per layer. The rounding happens in SQL so the accumulator stays a single atomic `UPDATE` (rounding in Python would reintroduce the read-before-write that deadlocks MariaDB and forces CockroachDB retries).
- **Fixed: `DELETE /filament/{id}` no longer fails outright on a filament with spools — now gated behind `cascade=true`** (#362) — the delete previously raised for *any* filament that still had spools, because the ORM had no cascade from filament to spool and tried (and failed) to null a `NOT NULL` foreign key on flush; there was no way to delete such a filament through the API at all. Deleting now explicitly cascades to the filament's spools and their usage history, but the endpoint refuses with **409** and states the exact spool count unless the caller passes `cascade=true` — deleting a filament with spools is unavoidably destructive and irreversible, so it is opt-in, not silent. A filament with no spools deletes exactly as before: no new required parameter, no behavior change for existing callers. The order-line hard refusal (#298/#320) is unaffected and `cascade` can never override it.
- **New: Scan-to-Spool — photograph a label, get a prefilled create form** (#361) — the scan dialog gains a **Photo** tab (phones open the camera directly; photos are downscaled in-browser before upload). The configured vision model reads the label into structured fields (vendor, name, material, weight, diameter, temperatures, lot number, article number — never guessing what it can't see), and Spoolman matches the result **against your own filament library first** (a known filament just gains a spool — no duplicate records), then the locally-synced [SpoolmanDB](https://github.com/Donkie/SpoolmanDB) catalog, with the raw extraction as an always-available fallback. The review step hands off to the normal create forms, prefilled and fully editable — nothing is created until you save. Photos are ephemeral by design: held in memory for the request, never written to disk, database, or logs. Extraction and matching are separate endpoints (`POST /api/v1/ai/spool-intake/extract`, `POST /api/v1/ai/spool-intake/match`) joined by a stable extraction-JSON contract, so a future companion app running an on-device vision model can reuse the same matching without any photo leaving the phone. Both endpoints answer 404 until the feature toggle is on.
- **New: AI provider foundation** (#359) — the shared plumbing every AI feature builds on, inert until configured: a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint config (env vars `SPOOLMAN_AI_BASE_URL`/`_API_KEY`/`_MODEL`/`_VISION_MODEL` are authoritative over the new **Settings → AI** tab; env-set fields show locked in the UI), provider presets as data (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Requesty, Groq, Mistral, Gemini), and a capability probe (`GET /api/v1/ai/status`, `POST /api/v1/ai/probe`) reporting reachability, the endpoint's model list, and honest per-capability verdicts — Ollama endpoints are enriched via Ollama's own API; generic endpoints report *not verified* rather than a guess. Feature toggles (all **off** by default) grey out with the reason inline when their requirements aren't met — e.g. Scan-to-Spool with a model that has no vision support. The API key is **write-only**: stored outside the settings registry (which echoes and broadcasts registered values), never returned by any endpoint, cleared or replaced but never shown. A stock install renders zero new UI outside the settings tab and sends nothing anywhere.
- **New: Home Assistant ingress support** (#211) — the server can now render the web UI for HA's embedded sidebar panel. With `SPOOLMAN_HA_INGRESS=1` (set only by the [HA add-on](https://github.com/sherrmann/spoolman-ng-addons)'s run script) the three path-dependent responses — index.html's asset paths, the PWA manifest's `start_url`/`scope`, and `/config.js` — are rendered per-request for the rotating per-session prefix HA passes in the `X-Ingress-Path` header (strictly validated before it is ever reflected; anything malformed falls back to the configured base path). Under ingress the client skips service-worker registration, since no SW scope can follow a rotating token path. Strictly additive: requests without the header — the direct host port, with the full PWA, QR deep links and API/websocket integrations — serve byte-identical bodies to before, and root/`SPOOLMAN_BASE_PATH` deployments outside HA are unchanged (the header is ignored entirely without the env flag). index.html, the manifest and `/config.js` are now served with `Cache-Control: no-store` in all modes so no cache can pin a dead session path. Covered end-to-end by a simulated ingress gateway in front of the real backend: boot, API, live-update websocket and token rotation inside the prefix, plus unchanged direct access on the same process.
- **New: per-install-type update action** (#294) — the "update available" hint (#293) is now clickable and opens a dialog tailored to how Spoolman was installed. **Native** installs get a real **Update now** button that runs the bundled `scripts/update.sh` in the background (under systemd the service restarts itself; otherwise the dialog says to restart manually). **Docker** installs get the `docker compose pull && up -d` steps plus an image-tag reminder; **Home Assistant** add-ons are pointed at Supervisor's own update UI. Triggering the updater from a browser is remote code execution by design, so the endpoint is **admin-only** whenever authentication is configured and, on an open (no-auth) instance, stays disabled unless `SPOOLMAN_ALLOW_UI_UPDATE=TRUE` is set explicitly; only the bundled script runs, and the sole caller input is an optional `--tag` validated against `^v[0-9.]+$`. `GET /api/v1/info` additively reports `install_type` and `update_action_available`.
- **New: from-scratch order builder** (#324) — the Orders page's **"+ New order"** button was a disabled placeholder; orders could only be born from the Low Stock flows (mark-as-ordered / bulk create). It now opens a builder that adds a filament picker + lines editor on top of the order details modal's header surface (shop, order date, order number, link, comment): pick any filaments, set each line's quantity and price, add/remove lines, and create the order in one step. Create is gated until at least one line has a filament chosen.
- **Removed: per-spool colour override** (revert of #74) — colour is an intrinsic property of a filament *product* (a red and a blue Sunlu PLA are different products), so it is modelled only on the filament. The per-spool override added a second, conflicting source of truth for the same attribute and forced every swatch surface — and every external API consumer — to know a `spool ?? filament` fallback rule. The three `spool` colour columns (`color_hex`, `multi_color_hexes`, `multi_color_direction`), the spool create/edit colour picker, and the API fields are gone; a migration drops the columns (any override a spool had stored is discarded — its swatch simply shows the filament colour, exactly as an unset override already did). The "different colour of the same filament" workflow is served by the filament **Clone** action instead. Integrations (Moonraker/OctoPrint/Home Assistant, NFC tags, the colour-similarity filter) were unaffected either way, since they always read the filament's colour.
- **New: deployment-catalog templates (Zeabur, Unraid, BigBear) + NAS-catalog docs** (#266) — submission-ready packaging for the Docker image now lives in-repo: `integrations/zeabur/` (one-click Zeabur template, SQLite default plus a PostgreSQL variant — each deployable into your own account with `npx zeabur@latest template deploy -f template.yaml`), `integrations/unraid/` (Unraid Docker-manager XML template with Unraid-appropriate defaults — appdata path, `PUID`/`PGID` 99/100 — usable today by dropping it into `templates-user/`, ready for a Community Apps listing), and `integrations/bigbear/` (compose entry in BigBear/CasaOS catalog conventions). The installation guide gains a one-click-catalogs section plus a TrueCharts/TrueNAS SCALE note: override the image repository to `ghcr.io/sherrmann/spoolman-ng` and keep everything else — port 8000, the data volume, `SPOOLMAN_*` env vars, the `/api/v1/health` probe — unchanged. The external catalog submissions are tracked per target: #335 (Zeabur marketplace), #336 (Unraid Community Apps), #337 (BigBear).
- **New: KIAUH v6 community extension** (#270) — KIAUH v5 had a built-in (upstream) Spoolman installer; v6 moved to community-maintained extensions, and `integrations/kiauh/` now ships one for Spoolman NG. From KIAUH's Extensions menu it installs the latest release zip natively into `~/Spoolman` (port prompt included), wires Moonraker — the `[update_manager Spoolman]` *type: zip* recipe (#263), the `[spoolman]` filament-tracking section, and the `moonraker.asvc` entry — and offers in-place update and clean remove (database preserved by default). One-liner to add it to a KIAUH clone: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sherrmann/Spoolman-NG/master/integrations/kiauh/install-extension.sh | bash`.
- **New: filament reference photos** (#88) — attach a photo to a filament (e.g. of the spool or the shop listing) so visually unusual filaments — glitter, transparent PETG — are easy to recognize. Uploaded via `PUT /filament/{id}/image` (raw JPEG/PNG/WebP body, 2 MB cap, no multipart) and served with ETag/304 caching from `GET /filament/{id}/image`; the filament payload gains a `has_image` flag. The browser downscales photos to ≤1024 px before upload and strips metadata such as GPS coordinates; bytes are stored as database blobs, so every existing backup path (SQLite rotation, external-DB dumps) captures them unchanged. The photo shows on the filament page and replaces the colour tile in the gallery view, with upload on the create and edit forms.
- **Fixed: order arrival is now one transaction** (#322) — arrival previously committed the line mutations first and then created each spool in its own commit, so a failure part-way through spool creation left lines marked arrived with only some of their spools and no way to retry (re-arrive rejects arrived lines). Line arrival and spool creation now commit together: any failure rolls the whole arrival back, so the order stays fully outstanding and can be arrived cleanly on retry.
- **Docs: RPi Imager integrations & compatibility matrix** (#315) — the README Integrations section now carries a table for the Raspberry Pi Imager **3D printing** catalog (OctoPi, OctoKlipperPi, Mainsail OS, PrintWatch OS, SimplyPrint, DuetPi, Repetier-Server, 3DPrinterOS), stating whether and how each appliance works with Spoolman, plus adjacent tools (Fluidd, KlipperScreen, Home Assistant, OctoEverywhere). Cross-links the sibling integration issues (#312–#314).

## [2026.7.14] — 2026-07-20

- **Reverted the unreleased filament 'ordered' fields** (#298/#309) — the three flat `ordered_at`/`order_url`/`order_note` columns that landed unreleased in #309 modelled order state as a property of a product type (couldn't group a bulk order, capture arrival into spools, or hold a shop). They are removed before any release wired them into the stable v1 API, and superseded by first-class **Orders & Shops** (Phase 1, below).
- **New: Shops** (#298) — a first-class `/shop` entity (name, homepage, region ships-to list, comment), distinct from the manufacturer Vendor, for tracking where filament is reordered.
- **New: Orders** (#298) — a `/order` entity grouping the lines of one bulk reorder (per-line filament, quantity, price). Order state (open/arrived) is derived from its lines; a PATCH with `lines` fully replaces the line set. Deleting an order cascades its lines; a shop with orders, or a filament with order lines, cannot be deleted — both reject the delete with **409 Conflict** and a message naming the references (#320), so clients key on one status for the referenced-cannot-delete case.
- **New: order arrival** (#298) — `POST /order/{id}/arrive` marks lines arrived and optionally turns the delivered quantities into spools (carrying each line's price and an optional location). Partial deliveries split a line into an arrived part and an outstanding remainder, so split shipments need no extra order states.
- **New: filament `on_order` field** (#298) — the filament list and detail endpoints now expose `on_order` = `{order_id, ordered_at}` of the oldest open order containing the filament (null when nothing is outstanding). Home Assistant / HACS automations can read it to quiet low-stock alerts once a replenishment is on its way.
- **Fixed: label preview now sits beside the settings** (#296) — a global layout rule (from the dashboard redesign) silently forced the print dialog's two columns to stack at every window size, leaving half the screen empty. Wide screens get preview + settings side by side; below ~1000 px they stack intentionally.
- **New: pre-print checklist** (#296) — clicking Print first shows the geometry checks that browser print dialogs commonly break: scale 100 % (never "fit to page"), the exact paper size in mm, margins off, headers/footers off. When a label paper size is used with automatic page sizing, a one-click "Match label size" fix is offered. Dismissible with "don't show again".
- **New: label QR size setting** (#295) — the printed QR square is now adjustable in mm from the label dialogs (Auto keeps the old fill-half-the-label behavior); a soft warning flags sizes under 10 mm as hard to phone-scan. Also fixes the QR overflowing its half of narrow labels: the SVG's intrinsic size no longer overrides the layout split.
- **Deployment-arc hardening**: upgrades now carry *data* in the tests (native update and `docker compose pull`-style image swap both prove pre-upgrade spools survive migrations); a new CI `verify-artifact` job runs the release-zip contract against the candidate artifact *before* anything publishes; the native install matrix gains an **arm64 (Pi-class) leg** under QEMU; third-party consumer checkouts auto-refresh weekly and suites log consumer versions; suites refresh the local `:latest` image once per session (stale caches silently tested old releases).

## [2026.7.13] — 2026-07-18

- **Image publishing polish** (#273) — multi-arch images now carry BuildKit **SBOM and provenance attestations**, and releases sync a proper overview to the Docker Hub page (`cookiemonster95/spoolman-ng`), which was previously blank.
- **Docs: reverse proxies & networking** (#275) — canonical recipes in the installation guide: Caddy, nginx (with the WebSocket upgrade headers live updates need), Traefik incl. sub-path via `SPOOLMAN_BASE_PATH`, auth-at-proxy caveats for printer traffic, IPv6 (`SPOOLMAN_HOST=::`), and a rootless-Podman quadlet unit.
- **New: `scripts/update.sh`** (#271) — one-command in-place updates for native installs without Moonraker: overlays the new release (preserving `.env`, `.venv`, `uv/`), re-syncs dependencies (keeping the NFC extra when present), seeds pip, and restarts the systemd service. Covered by an e2e that upgrades a real previous-release install.
- **New: official Helm chart** (#274) — published with every release as an OCI artifact: `helm install spoolman oci://ghcr.io/sherrmann/charts/spoolman-ng`. Single replica by design (SQLite is single-writer), PVC-backed data directory, health probes, non-root security context, `SPOOLMAN_*` env passthrough, optional secret-file database password, and ingress with `SPOOLMAN_BASE_PATH` support. Verified by a new k3d install test (`tests_deployment/run.sh helm`); chart lint runs in CI.

## [2026.7.12] — 2026-07-18

- **Fixed: Moonraker one-click updates were broken four ways** (#261–#264, found by the deployment-targets audit): `release_info.json` now names the GitHub repo exactly (`Spoolman-NG`) so Moonraker's update checks work — existing native installs need the one-time fix in the [migration note](docs/installation.md#one-click-updates-from-moonraker-klipper-users); release titles are now the bare tag so Moonraker stops showing a perpetual "update available"; the release zip ships a root `requirements.txt` and the installer seeds `pip` into `.venv`, enabling the newly documented `type: zip` updater recipe (dependency reinstalls + service restart) — the previous `type: web` recipe, which **wiped `.venv` and `.env` on first update**, is gone from the docs; and `scripts/*.sh` inside the zip are executable again, so the documented install one-liner works.
- **New: deployment-channel contract tests (Tier 1)** in `tests_deployment/` (#277) — a locally runnable harness (`tests_deployment/run.sh`) that exercises the published artifacts through their real consumers: the release-zip contract, `scripts/install.sh` on Debian/Fedora/Arch containers, **real Moonraker** validating the updater recipe via its own API, and the Home Assistant add-on options contract. Red assertions cite the issue they pin; `SPOOLMAN_ZIP_PATH` lets them verify unreleased artifacts.

## [2026.7.10] — 2026-07-11

- **Digital Asset Links: `handle_all_urls` served too** — Bitwarden (and other credential managers that validate app↔site association themselves) require the `handle_all_urls` relation in `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`; the server now serves both relations, so in-app passkey flows work with third-party credential managers as well.

## [2026.7.9] — 2026-07-11

- **Frictionless passkey setup**: the server now serves `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` itself (no manual reverse-proxy config), and the companion app gained an in-app **passkey setup assistant** that reads the app identity natively and walks through the domain association.
- **Companion app passkeys**: the login WebView supports WebAuthn ceremonies (via the WebView's `WEB_AUTHENTICATION_SUPPORT_FOR_APP` mode), so passkey login through a forward-auth portal (e.g. Authelia) works inside the app.
- **Companion app self-update (Android)**: the app checks GitHub releases and can download and install the release APK in-app.

## [2026.7.8] — 2026-07-10

- **Companion app: forward-auth gateways supported** — a server behind Authelia or a similar portal is detected during setup, and login completes through an in-WebView portal flow instead of a dead-end connection error.

## [2026.7.7] — 2026-07-10

- **Fixed: auth blocked every intended-open endpoint on real deployments.** With an API token or user accounts configured, `/api/v1/health`, `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/auth/status` and even `/auth/login` returned 401 — making password login impossible and breaking health monitoring. The middleware compared its sub-app-relative open-path list against the full request path (Starlette keeps the mount prefix in `root_path`); the unit harness drove the app unmounted, which is why tests stayed green. Found by the Home Assistant add-on live-testing round; now covered by mounted-app regression tests including `SPOOLMAN_BASE_PATH` prefixes.
- **Home Assistant add-on moved to a dedicated repository**: [`sherrmann/spoolman-ng-addons`](https://github.com/sherrmann/spoolman-ng-addons) — Supervisor requires the repository manifest at the git root, so the in-tree `ha-addon/` packaging could only ever be installed by manual copy. The add-on is now installable by URL from the HA add-on store, and every release pushes a matching version bump there so updates appear in the HA UI automatically.
- **API docs deploy fixed**: docs now deploy from master pushes — tag refs are blocked by the Pages environment.

## [2026.7.6] — 2026-07-10

- **Translations completed for every language**: the ~300 keys per locale that accumulated untranslated over the 2026.7.x feature wave (auth, printers, locations, statistics, weigh workflow, bulk edit, …) are now translated in all locales, with correct language-specific plural forms. CI now enforces **placeholder integrity** — a translation that drops a `{{variable}}` or `<tag>` fails the build (this immediately caught 34 stale/broken values, now fixed).
- **UK English added and made the default**: `en-GB` (British spellings, UK date formats) is used unless the browser or the user picks another language; the previous `en` remains available as *English (US)* — and its date pickers now consistently use US formats instead of the old US-strings/UK-formats mix.
- **Home dashboard**: the redundant page title/subtitle is gone; the "Value" KPI is now an honest **estimated stock value** (spool price falling back to filament price, scaled by remaining weight — previously it summed only explicit spool prices); the filament KPI footer shows the distinct material count instead of the meaningless "all synced".
- **Spool list**: the totals row is always visible and sums the **selected** spools when a selection exists (otherwise the shown page); *Show Archived* now shows **only** archived spools (new `archived` query filter on `GET /api/v1/spool`); the bulk bar offers Archive or Unarchive to match the active view; the filament-name link uses the normal text colour; toolbar buttons have tooltips; *Hide Columns* is now *Columns*.
- **Colour filter**: leads with a one-click palette of common filament colours (full picker behind *More colors*), and the toolbar button shows the active colour.
- **Spool page**: a summary card with swatch, tags, stock bar and key numbers; a *Sibling spools* header button that lists every spool of the same filament; adjusting filament now refreshes the usage history immediately.
- **Filament list**: aligned with the spool list — inline editing (material, price, article number, comment), a colour-tile grid view, the Columns manager with drag-to-reorder/resize, and toolbar tooltips.
- **Label printing**: the live preview warns when label content is clipped or the grid cannot fit the paper.
- **Home Assistant add-on**: fixed the base image name (`spoolman-ng`) so the add-on actually builds; `poe bump` now keeps the add-on version in step; documented the working local-add-on install path.
- **Release pipeline**: images/releases now require the unit, client and e2e suites to pass; API docs redeploy on release tags.

## [2026.7.0] – [2026.7.5] — 2026-07

Six releases; full auto-generated notes on the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/sherrmann/Spoolman-NG/releases) page. Highlights:

- **Repository renamed to [`sherrmann/Spoolman-NG`](https://github.com/sherrmann/Spoolman-NG).** Old `github.com/sherrmann/Spoolman` links — including existing Moonraker `repo:` entries — keep working through GitHub's redirects. The API docs moved to <https://sherrmann.github.io/Spoolman-NG/> with **no** redirect from the old address.
- **Docker images renamed** to `ghcr.io/sherrmann/spoolman-ng` and `cookiemonster95/spoolman-ng`. The old `ghcr.io/sherrmann/spoolman` / `cookiemonster95/spoolman` images stay pullable but are frozen at the last tag published before the rename — update the `image:` line in your compose file; data volumes and settings are unaffected.
- **Optional user accounts** (password login, admin/read-only roles), API tokens, and an experimental Home Assistant add-on package.
- **Locations** as a first-class entity with custom fields, scannable location labels and scan-to-move; **printer** entity with spool assignment.
- **List upgrades**: free-text search, colour-similarity filter, bulk edit/archive, weigh-spools workflow, drag-to-reorder/resize columns, hue sorting, totals row, grid view, inline editing, unit auto-scaling.
- **Spool intelligence**: usage & cost statistics (`/api/v1/stats/usage`), per-spool usage-event history and weight-history chart, per-spool colour/diameter overrides, idempotent use/measure endpoints.
- **Filament & import**: slicer-profile export, sliced-`.3mf` bulk adjust, retail-barcode lookup, SpoolmanDB catalog descriptors, temperature ranges.
- The client bundle is now built inside the Dockerfile, so `docker build .` works from a clean checkout.

## [2026.6.0] — 2026-06-30

First release of the Spoolman NG fork, built on upstream Spoolman 0.23.1.

- **NFC spool identification** — TigerTag, OpenPrintTag, and QIDI tags. Included in the Docker images for all architectures (`amd64`, `arm64`, `armv7`).
- **Filament label printing** with separate presets, QR codes, and filament QR scanning support.
- **Redesigned home dashboard** with KPI cards and inventory analytics.
- Merged upstream community PRs: extra-field filter/sort, 3D Filament Profiles import, weight-delta events, and calibration.
- **Fork infrastructure**: multi-arch images published to GHCR (`ghcr.io/sherrmann/spoolman`) and Docker Hub (`cookiemonster95/spoolman`); CalVer releases with `:latest`, `:edge`, and `:sha-*` tags; and one-click updates via Moonraker's `update_manager`.
